author: Robert Hart
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/akrales_220309_4977_0232-1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Are legions of smart devices - fridges, ovens, vacuum cleaners, lawnmowers, security cameras, and TVs - conspiring to take over the internet? No. But they could soon be unwitting hosts to self-replicating AI models that spread from device to device and prove remarkably difficult to contain.

Welcome to the unsettling world of AI worms, where, depending on who you ask, the prospect of models spreading uncontrollably across household appliances is either an imminent cybersecurity risk or another case of AI companies spreading doomer-tinged hype. title: (No AI) Epic’s new games launcher is ‘vibe coded’
author: Jay Peters
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/New-Epic-Games-Launcher-2.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Epic Games is announcing a big refresh of its PC games launcher today in preview, saying that the new version is "way faster" and now supports Linux. But the company, which has been publicly making a big push into AI-assisted development, also notes that the refresh was "vibe coded."

"Programming is hard," [Epic says in a blog post](https://store.epicgames.com/news/epic-games-launcher-preview). "So, instead of doing that, we vibe coded a new Epic Games Launcher that's way faster and more responsive than the current one, and has a new look."

On Monday, CEO Tim Sweeney [announced that](https://x.com/TimSweeneyEpic/status/2109705826688549304) the company has a "huge pivot underway," where it will be "moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration. …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/games/1010751/epic-games-launcher-vibe-coded-ai-linux)
